title: Coins after the villa
place: Llandough hill: the empty villa south of the future church, and the ground north of it
sources: media register MR-0096 / MR-0097 (Holbrook & Thomas 2005, 'An Early-medieval Monastic Cemetery at Llandough, Glamorgan: Excavations in 1994', Medieval Archaeology 49), p. 86 (later coins and pottery in grave fills; villa abandoned in the first third of the 4th century; 'conceivable … another Roman building beneath the churchyard') and p. 88 (earliest burial 370–640 cal AD)

shots.direction: Dusk: the villa house south of the future churchyard, roof partly fallen, rooms empty; slow drift right.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9, late Roman Britain, late 4th century. Wide dusk shot: a modest single-range Romano-British stone house on an inland hilltop in south-east Wales, roof tiles partly fallen, doorways dark and empty, grass in the yard; below, a winding river and reed marshes. No people. No mosaics, no church, no crosses. No text, no lettering, no heraldry or emblems, no modern objects, invented faces only, no likeness of any real person.

captions.text: The villa house had been left in the first third of the 4th century

shots.direction: Close: a worn bronze coin and a sherd of late Roman pottery pressed into the turf north of the old house.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 macro: a small worn late Roman bronze coin and a sherd of grey Roman pottery half-pressed into wet turf and red clay; shallow depth of field, soft evening light. No text, no lettering, no heraldry or emblems, no modern objects, invented faces only, no likeness of any real person.

captions.text: Later coins and pottery than the villa's own were found in the graves dug here centuries afterwards

shots.direction: High wide: the ground immediately north of where the churchyard will be, empty grass to the escarpment edge; small coin-glints in the turf.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9, late Roman Britain. High wide view of an empty grassy hill crest falling to a steep scarp above a river estuary, late afternoon; no people, no buildings in the foreground. No text, no lettering, no heraldry or emblems, no modern objects, invented faces only, no likeness of any real person.

captions.text: These finds lay in the ground north of today's churchyard, clustered at its southern edge. Whether another Roman building stood there is not known
Source: Holbrook & Thomas 2005 (MR-0097): 'conceivable', unproven. The site records nothing for the hill between this and the first graves.
